tax.text:
We are subject to income taxes in the United States and in various state and foreign jurisdictions. Determining our income tax provision requires significant judgment, including estimates of future taxable income and the interpretation and application of complex tax laws and regulations that differ by jurisdiction and are subject to change.

During the course of the fiscal year, we apply an estimated annual effective tax rate to year-to-date pre-tax income, excluding infrequently occurring or unusual items, and we record the tax effects of the infrequent or unusual items in the period in which they occur. As the fiscal year progresses, we update our rate estimate for actual results and revised forecasts of income by jurisdiction, and any change in estimate is reflected in the quarter in which it is made.

We recognize the benefit of an uncertain tax position only if it is more likely than not to be sustained upon examination. We reassess these positions each quarter as audits progress, statutes of limitations expire, and tax laws or other circumstances change, which can result in a tax benefit or additional expense in the period of the change.

We establish valuation allowances for deferred tax assets when we estimate it is more likely than not that the tax assets will not be realized.

sbc.heading: Stock-Based Compensation
sbc.text:
Our shareholders have approved a performance-based long-term incentive plan that provides for grants of stock-based performance awards to certain managerial personnel and executive management as directed by the Organization and Compensation Committee of the Board of Directors. Under the terms of some equity awards, the number of common shares that are vested and issued to participants is variable and is based upon the achievement of specified performance objectives during defined service periods. Due to the variable number of common shares that may be issued under some of our equity awards, we reevaluate our performance-award grants on a quarterly basis and adjust the number of shares expected to be awarded based upon actual and estimated financial results of the Company compared with the performance goals set for the award. Adjustments to the number of shares expected to vest, and to the corresponding compensation expense, are made on a cumulative basis at the adjustment date based upon the new estimated probable number of common shares to be awarded.

The analysis of our performance awards contains uncertainties because we are required to make assumptions and judgments about the timing and/or the eventual number of shares that will vest in each grant.

We regularly review the collectability assumptions of our allowance for credit losses calculation and compare them against historical collections. Adjustments to the assumptions may either increase or decrease our total allowance for credit losses and may adversely impact our financial results. For example, a 10% increase to our allowance for credit losses at August 31, 2026, would decrease our reported income from operations by $0.2 million.

net sales.text:
We account for revenue in accordance with Accounting Standards Update No. 2014-09, Revenue from Contracts with Customers (Topic 606) . For the All Access Pass, judgment is required to determine whether the intellectual property and web-based functionality and content are considered distinct and accounted for separately, or not distinct and accounted for together.

We have determined to account for the AAP as a single performance obligation and recognize the associated transaction price ratably over the term of the underlying contract beginning on the commencement date of each contract, which is the date the Company’s platforms and resources are made available to the customer. This determination was reached after considering that our web-based functionality and content, in combination with our intellectual property, each represent inputs that transform into a combined output that represents the intended outcome of the AAP, which is to provide a continuously accessible, customized, and dynamic learning and development solution only accessible through the AAP platform.

Judgment is required to determine the stand-alone selling price (SSP) for each distinct performance obligation in a revenue contract. Where we have more than one distinct performance obligation, we must allocate the transaction price to each performance obligation based on its relative SSP.

s.t: No customer accounted for more than 10% of our sales or accounts receivable in any year presented.
Our ability to help clients achieve results that require changes in human behavior depends on the capability, engagement, and durability of our own workforce.

Our business depends on renewals of subscription-based offerings and sales of new subscription-based services for a significant portion of our revenue, and our failure to renew at sufficient rates or generate new sales of such offerings will lead to a decrease in our revenues.

A large portion of our success depends on our ability to generate renewals of our subscription-based offerings, which primarily consist of the AAP and Leader in Me membership, and produce new sales of our offerings and products to both new and existing clients.
Our success depends on our ability to maintain and enhance our brand image and reputation.

Maintaining, promoting, and growing our brands will depend on our design and marketing efforts, including advertising and consumer campaigns, content and platform innovation and quality, and our efforts in these respects may not have the desired impact on our brand image and reputation.

In addition, our success in maintaining, extending, and expanding our brand image depends on our ability to adapt to a rapidly changing media environment, including our increasing reliance on social media and digital dissemination of advertising campaigns on our digital platforms and through our digital experiences.
Our brand value also depends on our ability to maintain a positive consumer perception of our corporate integrity, purpose, and brand culture.
To protect our intellectual property, we rely upon a combination of confidentiality policies, nondisclosure and other contractual arrangements, as well as copyright and trademark laws.
We depend on key personnel, the loss of whom could harm our business.
Our future success also depends on our ability to identify, attract, and retain additional qualified senior personnel.
Our subscription-based offerings depend on the availability, performance, security, and reliability of our technology platforms and related infrastructure.

We also rely on third parties for cloud hosting, data storage and processing, telecommunications, software, artificial intelligence technologies, cybersecurity services, and other important functions.

Our ability to make scheduled payments on or to refinance any indebtedness depends on our future performance, including the performance of our subsidiaries, which will be affected by financial, business and economic conditions, competition, and other factors.

The actual timing, number, and value of common shares purchased under our board-approved purchase plan will be determined at our discretion and will depend on a number of factors, including, among others, general market and business conditions, the trading price of common shares, and applicable legal requirements.
Our primary sources of liquidity are cash flows from the sale of services and products in the normal course of business and available proc eeds from our credit facility.
Our primary source of cash from operating activities was the sale of services and products to our customers in the normal course of business.
Given these risks and uncertainties, investors should not rely on forward-looking statements as a prediction of actual results.

gp.text: Gross Profit. Gross profit decreased $7.0 million to $115.6 million in fiscal 2026 compared with $122.6 million in the prior fiscal year, due to both decreased revenue and lower gross margin. North America segment gross margin declined to 81.1% of revenue in fiscal 2026 compared with 83.1% in the prior year. The decrease in gross margin was primarily due to a change in the mix of products sold, increased delivery costs during the fiscal year, and increased amortization of capitalized curriculum expense.

cor.text: Gross pr ofit consists of net revenue less the cost of services provided or the cost of goods sold. Our cost of revenue includes the direct costs of delivering content onsite at client locations, including presenter costs; content royalties; materials used in the production of training products and related assessments; amortization of previously capitalized curriculum development costs; and freight. Gross profit may be affected by, among other things, the mix of services sold to clients, prices of materials, travel, labor rates, changes in product discount levels, and freight costs. Our consolidated cost of revenue in fiscal 2026 totaled $65.4 million compared with $63.5 million in the prior year. Consolidated gross profit for the fiscal year ended August 31, 2026 was $196.0 million compared with $203.6 million in fiscal 2025 and decreased primarily due to lower revenue as described above. Our gross margin for fiscal 2026 decreased to 75.0% compared with 76.2% in the prior year primarily due to changes in the mix of products sold during the year, increased delivery costs, and increased amortization of capitalized curriculum expense.

opex.text: Our operating expenses for the year ended August 31, 2026 decreased $9.0 million to $188.9 million, compared with $197.9 million in the prior year. The decrease was primarily due to a $7.2 million decline in selling, general, and administrative (SG&A) expenses and a $1.9 million decrease in amortization expense. Decreased SG&A expense was primarily due to a $4.4 million decrease in associate expenses resulting from our restructuring activities during fiscal 2026 and in prior years, and cost reduction efforts in various areas of our business. We incurred $6.7 million of restructuring expenses in fiscal 2026, which was consistent with spending in the prior year. We are currently in a long-term restructuring plan and expect to incur additional restructuring costs in fiscal 2027. Our amortization expense from definite-lived intangible assets decreased primarily due to a re-evaluation of the useful lives of intangible assets generated from the merger with the Covey Leadership Center, which continue to be some of our primary revenue and cash generating assets. During fiscal 2026, we extended the lives of these intangible assets by approximately 5 years, which reduced our amortization expense when compared with the prior year.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
We are subject to income taxes in the United States and in various state and foreign jurisdictions. Determining our income tax provision requires significant judgment, including estimates of future taxable income and the interpretation and application of complex tax laws and regulations that differ by jurisdiction and are subject to change.

During the course of the fiscal year, we apply an estimated annual effective tax rate to year-to-date pre-tax income, excluding infrequently occurring or unusual items, and we record the tax effects of the infrequent or unusual items in the period in which they occur. As the fiscal year progresses, we update our rate estimate for actual results and revised forecasts of income by jurisdiction, and any change in estimate is reflected in the quarter in which it is made.

We recognize the benefit of an uncertain tax position only if it is more likely than not to be sustained upon examination. We reassess these positions each quarter as audits progress, statutes of limitations expire, and tax laws or other circumstances change, which can result in a tax benefit or additional expense in the period of the change.

We establish valuation allowances for deferred tax assets when we estimate it is more likely than not that the tax assets will not be realized.

Our Adjusted EBITDA in fiscal 2026 increased slightly to $28.9 million compared with $28.8 million in the prior year, reflecting the above-noted factors. In constant currency, our fiscal 2026 Adjusted EBITDA was $28.6 million. Adjusted EBITDA and constant currency are non-GAAP financial measures. For additional information regarding our use of non-GAAP f inancial measures, see the discussion under the heading Non-GAAP Measures above.

da.text: This Management’s Discussion and Analysis includes the concepts of adjusted earnings before interest, income taxes, depreciation, and amortization (Adjusted EBITDA) and “constant currency,” which are non-GAAP measures. We define Adjusted EBITDA as net income excluding the impact of interest, income taxes, definite-lived intangible asset amortization, depreciation, stock-based compensation expense, and certain other items such as restructuring charges and building exit costs. Constant currency is a non-GAAP financial measure that removes the impact of fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates and is calculated by translating the current period’s financial results at the same average exchange rates in effect during the prior year and then comparing this amount to the prior year.

sbc.heading: Stock-Based Compensation
sbc.text:
Our shareholders have approved a performance-based long-term incentive plan that provides for grants of stock-based performance awards to certain managerial personnel and executive management as directed by the Organization and Compensation Committee of the Board of Directors. Under the terms of some equity awards, the number of common shares that are vested and issued to participants is variable and is based upon the achievement of specified performance objectives during defined service periods. Due to the variable number of common shares that may be issued under some of our equity awards, we reevaluate our performance-award grants on a quarterly basis and adjust the number of shares expected to be awarded based upon actual and estimated financial results of the Company compared with the performance goals set for the award. Adjustments to the number of shares expected to vest, and to the corresponding compensation expense, are made on a cumulative basis at the adjustment date based upon the new estimated probable number of common shares to be awarded.

The analysis of our performance awards contains uncertainties because we are required to make assumptions and judgments about the timing and/or the eventual number of shares that will vest in each grant.

wc.heading: Accounts Receivable Valuation
wc.text:
Trade accounts receivable are recorded at the invoiced amount and do not bear interest. Our allowance for credit losses calculation contains uncertainties because the calculation requires us to make assumptions and judgments regarding the collectability of customer accounts, which may be influenced by a number of factors that are not within our control, such as the financial health of each customer. We regularly review the collectability assumptions of our allowance for credit losses calculation and compare them against historical collections. Adjustments to the assumptions may either increase or decrease our total allowance for credit losses and may adversely impact our financial results. For example, a 10% increase to our allowance for credit losses at August 31, 2026, would decrease our reported income from operations by $0.2 million.

For further information regarding the calculation of our allowance for credit losses, refer to the notes to our financial statements as presented in Item 8 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

net sales.heading: Revenue Recognition
net sales.text:
We account for revenue in accordance with Accounting Standards Update No. 2014-09, Revenue from Contracts with Customers (Topic 606) . For the All Access Pass, judgment is required to determine whether the intellectual property and web-based functionality and content are considered distinct and accounted for separately, or not distinct and accounted for together.

We have determined to account for the AAP as a single performance obligation and recognize the associated transaction price ratably over the term of the underlying contract beginning on the commencement date of each contract, which is the date the Company’s platforms and resources are made available to the customer. This determination was reached after considering that our web-based functionality and content, in combination with our intellectual property, each represent inputs that transform into a combined output that represents the intended outcome of the AAP, which is to provide a continuously accessible, customized, and dynamic learning and development solution only accessible through the AAP platform.

Judgment is required to determine the stand-alone selling price (SSP) for each distinct performance obligation in a revenue contract. Where we have more than one distinct performance obligation, we must allocate the transaction price to each performance obligation based on its relative SSP.
